title: Sell Mineral Rights in Taylor, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Taylor, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Taylor, ND east of Dickinson? Get a fair, informed look at what a Stark County flank interest is really worth.
heroLead: Taylor sits east of Dickinson along the Heart River, and the mineral interests held by families here tend to be modest, quiet, and easy to underestimate.
intro: There's less oil-and-gas headline activity around Taylor than in the western part of Stark County, but that doesn't mean nothing's ever happened here. We've seen Taylor-area tracts with old conventional leases and occasional Bakken-flank interest, and the only way to know what applies to your family's specific parcel is to check.

sections.heading: Heart River valley ground and its lease history
paragraphs: Farmland along the Heart River near Taylor was leased at various points as exploration moved through this part of the state, and some of those leases produced modest amounts of oil before going quiet. We check whether any lease on your tract is still active before we make an offer.

sections.heading: Confirming what you actually own
paragraphs: Because ownership here often traces back through several generations of the same family, we start by confirming your legal description and current ownership through the Stark County Recorder's office, so any offer reflects your real, current interest.

sections.heading: Why a careful look beats a quick guess
paragraphs: Taylor doesn't come up often in conversations about North Dakota oil, and that lack of attention means fewer buyers bother researching it properly. We'd rather spend the time checking your actual well and lease history than hand you a number based on a general sense of the county.
If your interest turns out to have real value, we want you to know that clearly; if it doesn't right now, we'll tell you that too, honestly.

faqs.question: We've never seen any activity on our Taylor property. Is it worth checking?
faqs.answer: Yes, checking costs nothing, and some Taylor-area tracts have lease history the current owners aren't aware of.

faqs.question: How do we find out if an old family lease is still valid?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever paperwork you have and we'll check the Stark County Recorder's records to determine the lease's current status.

faqs.question: What if we only inherited a fraction of the original interest?
faqs.answer: That's common. We'll confirm your exact decimal share before making an offer so it reflects only what you actually own.

faqs.question: Nobody nearby seems to know much about oil activity around Taylor. Should we trust that?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Limited local awareness doesn't mean limited value. We check the actual state records for your tract rather than rely on general impressions.
